title: Bug report: strict single-precision floating point comparisons (flt.s) may return 1 even though the operands are equal
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv.

## Brief bug description

The instruction `flt.s` must return `0` when the two operands are equal. Under certain conditions, it returns `1` even though the operands are equal.

## Example instance

### Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  li t0, 0xFFFFFFFF
  fcvt.s.wu	ft0,t0,rtz

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld ft1, 0(t0)

  // Here, ft0 = ft1 = 0xffffffff4f7fffff

  flt.s	t0,ft1,ft0

  li t2, 0x10
  sw t0, 0(t2)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff4f7fffff
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `t0 = 0`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `t0 = 1`.

## Notes

This issue has commonalities with #316 . The FPU seems to have a strict ordering between the two floating-point registers, which are in fact equal.

Thanks!
Flavien

Thanks :D

title: CJALR with instr[14:12] != 0 is not illegal
body:
The decoder for CJALR will not raise an illegal instruction exception when `instr[14:12] != 0`, but it will also not set `cheri_jalr_en`:

https://github.com/microsoft/cheriot-ibex/blob/3f0ec8600cb7621c4c952951d211b3515116ea27/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv#L343-L367

When a CJALR instruction is run with `instr[14:12] != 0`, the instruction that runs becomes one which stores the next instruction PC to the register file, but does not branch, since it runs into the old logic for JALR. This is therefore not a security issue, but is a bug.

Instead `illegal_insn` should be set when `instr[14:12] != 0` (see the original code for JALR, which does the same).

title: PoR value of MSTATUS
body:
### Bug Description

The [documented](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/doc/03_reference/cs_registers.rst?plain=1#LL109C1-L109C1) power-on-reset value of the `mstatus` CSR (0x300) is 0x0000_1800 which expands to:

| Bit Pos  | PoR | Field     |
| ------- | ----- | -------------- |
| 21    | 1'b0  | **TW**  |
| 17    | 1'b0 | **MPRV**  |
| 12:11 | 2'b11  | **MPP**  |
| 7     | 1'b0  | **MPIE** |
| 3     | 1'b0  | **MIE**  |

However the coded PoR in the [RTL](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/rtl/cve2_cs_registers.sv#L745) is:
```
localparam status_t MSTATUS_RST_VAL = '{mie:  1'b0,
                                          mpie: 1'b1,
                                          mpp:  PRIV_LVL_U,
                                          mprv: 1'b0,
                                          tw:   1'b0};
```
Given that [PRIV_LVL_U](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/blob/b8c94a3e84087e230581fcdddadbea398ea19a7e/rtl/cve2_pkg.sv#L206) is 2'b00, this yields a PoR of 0x0000_0080.

I believe that the documented PoR value is the proper one, but the coded PoR has been in the Ibex code for three years so I am not certain.

You can show this in simulation in CORE-V-VERIF by running the `debug_test`:
```
$ make test TEST=debug_test
```
(Set the SIMULATOR and USE_ISS vars as appropriate for your installation.)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: fix #128 power-on-reset value for MSTATUS CSR

comments.body: Note that the lowRISC team has determined that for Ibex, this is a _documentation_ bug, not an RTL bug.  See [Ibex Issue #2054](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/2054).  While I agree with their interpretation, I recommend we treat this as an RTL issue and proceed with @szbieg's update in [CVE2 pull-request #129](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cve2/pull/129/files).  This will align the PoR state of the CVE2 cores with the CV32E40 cores.

body:
Hi,

Shouldn't this be opposite ? 
https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/78c1751c4781ffe156128748810ee4af85fee058/litex/soc/cores/dma.py#L19-L20

Just to try this out I used the `WishboneDMAReader` in a module of my SoC (with vexriscv) simulation to read a word from SRAM and print it in my C code and it printed reversed. The complete system is little endian.
```
DMA Read from : 0x10003fac
Readback from DMA: 0xdf0feca
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

with the format_bytes reversed
```python
 def format_bytes(s, endianness): 
     return {"little": s, "big": reverse_bytes(s)}[endianness]
```
the print is as expected

```

Readback from DMA: 0xcafef00d
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

comments.body:
Hi @navaneeth-cirel,

this probably similar to https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litedram/issues/251. There is a endianness mismatch between the model and real hardware. I'll try to address this soon.

Hi @enjoy-digital ,

After brief look at the issue referenced it seems that there is a mismatch between the simulation and target hardware, but in my case I am seeing the mismatch in Simulation itself.
Just to give more clarity , what I am doing is writing a 32bit value to a `uint32_t` variable in the C code and set its address to the DMA to read and transfer to a CSR status register which I am then reading and printing in the C code, where the mismatch is observed.

I re-checked the current code and your observation still makes sense for a direct word-level use of `WishboneDMAReader`.

For a little-endian CPU writing `0xcafef00d` as a `uint32_t`, the Wishbone word read back by the DMA is already `0xcafef00d`. Passing `endianness="little"` to `WishboneDMAReader` then applies `reverse_bytes()`, so a direct word consumer such as a CSR status register will see `0x0df0feca`.

So for raw word-oriented use, the DMA should be instantiated with `endianness="big"` / no byte swap.

I would avoid flipping the global `format_bytes()` mapping since the DMA is also used in byte-stream storage paths, where this conversion is part of the expected byte ordering. The real issue is that the parameter is confusing for direct word users, so we should probably document this better and/or add a clearer no-swap/raw mode in the future.

This has now been improved with:  c4baeb3e1a3a35ecaa3e47eae4d2951b64d76bdd

The existing DMA endianness behavior is kept for compatibility: `endianness="little"` still byte-swaps and `endianness="big"` still preserves the raw Wishbone word.

To make direct word-oriented use cases clearer, `WishboneDMAReader` and `WishboneDMAWriter` now also have an explicit `with_byteswap` override. So for a raw word transfer such as the `0xcafef00d` case discussed here, the DMA can now be instantiated with:

```python
  WishboneDMAReader(bus, endianness="little", with_byteswap=False)
```

This preserves the raw Wishbone word instead of byte-swapping it.

I also added regression coverage for the reported word-level case on both reader and writer, checking both the legacy little-endian byte-swap behavior and the explicit no-swap path.

I also added a follow-up test commit to double-check the default behavior: https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/commit/db2678d1a2df8f47c76510fec134c4a093cf45cc

This adds regression coverage for the storage-style byte-stream path used by LiteSDCard/LiteSATA, where DMA words are converted to/from 8-bit streams with reverse stream converters.

The tests confirm why the legacy default remains unchanged for these users, while raw word-oriented users can use the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override added above.

With the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override and the added regression tests for both raw word and byte-stream DMA paths, I think this is now covered. Closing, but please reopen or open a follow-up if another DMA endianness case still behaves unexpectedly.

body:

```scala

  idcodeManufId = 0,
debugIdleCycles = 5) // Reasonable guess for synchronization.
```

Should the default IDCODE be 0x1, or the same as in the previous debug module (0x10e31913)? Or should it throw an error message to prevent rocket from elaborating if the JTAG is enabled but the idcode is not specified?

@mwachs5 @palmer-dabbelt @ducky64

comments.body:
The IDCODE (0x10e31913) uses SiFive's assigned JEDEC Manufacturer ID. So in general those who aren't SiFive should not be using that IDCODE. That's why we removed it from the default.

Those using rocket-chip repo should probably override this default value to something meaningful for their design. The ManufId is actually exported from the ExampleTop as part of its I/O and is tied off in the TestHarness.

I see, that makes sense. Thanks for the explanation. Would having an elaboration-time warning for users of rocket-chip be useful so that they don't run into surprises when they try to program their cores?

When you say "program their cores" do you mean when using OpenOCD to communicate with them? Is there actually a value that you use there that causes a problem? riscv-openocd is very tolerant of the IDCODE, it may print a warning if it's not the expected ID.

I'm not sure what the elaboration time warning would be because the mfr_id could go all the way out the pins of the chip. I added a runtime warning (so if you ran with simulate it could at least detect illegal idcodes, though the chances you detect an unconnected mfr_id are somewhat low):

https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/jtag/JtagTap.scala#L175

Note that if you did actually use the defaults here, then your IDCODE *would* be 0x1, because there is a bit in the IDCODE "always 1":
https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L230

@mwachs5 Ah, I see. I think I see where my confusion was coming from now.

In https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/9002e7e53299598027f41b95dba1666310923699/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L231 it uses two out of the three `Int`s in `JtagDTMConfig` but doesn't actually 
use the third one. I was confused since I thought that all 3 would be determined at elaboration-time by `JtagDTMConfig`. In my design, I think I left io.jtag_mfr_id unconnected and the synthesis tool tied it at some point to zero.

Perhaps if we are not actually going to use `c.idcodeManufId.U`, perhaps it could be a good idea to put in a comment saying "Please wire up io.jtag_mfr_id to set the mfr_id or something"? The TestHarness I think manually goes and re-retrieves it (or maybe just remove `idcodeManufId` from `JtagDTMConfig` to avoid confusion perhaps).

```scala
  idcode.always1    := 1.U
  idcode.version    := c.idcodeVersion.U
  idcode.partNumber := c.idcodePartNum.U
  idcode.mfrId := io.jtag_mfr_id
```

The comment seems like a reasonable request. Keep in mind that RocketChipExampleTop is just an example top level, and other designs could actually wire up mfrId using the value in JtagDTMConfig,  I think we should leave it there but comment it as you suggest.

title: Bug report: dependent arithmetic/muldiv single-precision operations cause wrong output by more than +1 or -1
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv, similar to #315 but the mismatch may be larger than +1 or -1.

## Brief bug description

A pair of dependent single-precision floating arithmetic/muldiv operations (not necessarily immediately following each other), provides wrong results in some cases, differing from the expectation by potentially a magnitude above 1.

I ran this code on master (b29eb54) where I cherry-picked the fix 5f67075, with the configuration described in #318 .

## Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld fa2, (t0)
  la t0, .fdata1
  fld ft7, (t0)

  fdiv.s	fs0,ft7,fa2,rmm
  fmul.s	fa2,fs0,fa2,rdn

  li t0, 0x18
  fsd fa2, 0(t0)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff5f4135ef # fa2
.section ".fdata1","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff98e7d58f # ft7
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `fa2= 0xffffffff98e7b3ae`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `fa2 = 0xffffffff98e7d58f`.

Thanks!
Flavien

title: [BUG] UnalignQueue "enqPtr < deqPtr" assertion triggered by cross-16B sd under sbuffer-stride pressure
body:
### Before start

- [x] I have read the [RISC-V ISA Manual](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual) and this is not a RISC-V ISA question. 我已经阅读过 RISC-V 指令集手册，这不是一个指令集本身的问题。
- [x] I have read the [XiangShan Documents](https://xiangshan-doc.readthedocs.io/zh_CN/latest). 我已经阅读过香山文档。
- [x] I have searched the previous issues and did not find anything relevant. 我已经搜索过之前的 issue，并没有找到相关的。
- [x] I have reviewed the commit messages from the relevant commit history. 我已经浏览过相关的提交历史和提交信息。
- [x] I have reproduced the incorrect behaviors using the latest commit on the master branch. 我已经使用 master 分支最新的 commit 复现了不正确的行为。

### Branch

kunminghu-v3

### Describe the bug

A short loop of cross-16B `sd` stores with unique-line stride deterministically fires the assertion at `NewStoreQueue.scala:1414` inside the inner `UnalignQueue` module:

```scala
XSError(enqPtr < deqPtr && !full, s"Something wrong in UnalignQueue!")
```

```
[0] %Error: UnalignQueue.sv:139: Assertion failed in
    TOP.SimTop.cpu.l_soc.core_with_l2.core.memBlock.inner_lsq.storeQueue.unalignQueue:
    Assertion failed at LogUtils.scala:132
%Error: build/rtl/UnalignQueue.sv:139: Verilog $stop
Aborting...
```

The reproducer (200 iterations, two cross-16B `sd`s per iteration, 32-byte stride) fires the assertion deterministically within 5,000 cycles (5/5 reruns). Halving the iteration count, removing the stride, removing the second `sd`, or aligning the base address each makes the assertion not fire in the same cycle window.

### Expected behavior

`UnalignQueue` should maintain its `enqPtr` / `deqPtr` invariant under any legal sequence of cross-16B stores, regardless of sbuffer occupancy or loop-trip count.

### Environment

- Hardware
  - CPU: Intel Xeon Platinum 8592+
  - Memory (GB): 1006
  - Storage (GB): 2000
- Software
  - Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
  - gcc version: 13.2.0
  - clang version: -
  - java version: openjdk 21.0.10
  - mill version: 0.12.15
- Repo
  - XiangShan commit id: `cc942e98c8fdd4b0ad3a8bddc9bfbd125b1f5d81`
  - difftest commit id: `f9d0bb858c18133984a5efd476f59989c69cb23f`
  - NEMU commit id: not used (`--no-diff`)
  - SPIKE commit id: not used
- Build & Run
  - Build command: `make sim-verilog && make -C ./difftest emu NUM_CORES=1 RTL_SUFFIX=sv`
  - Run command: `./build/verilator-compile/emu --no-diff -i unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin -C 5000`

### To Reproduce

Run the attached binary:

```
./build/verilator-compile/emu --no-diff -i unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin -C 5000
```

The assertion fires deterministically before 5,000 cycles (5/5 reruns).

The full reproducer is 9 instructions:

```assembly
_start:
  li   s2, 200                  # iteration count
  li   t0, 0x8010000F           # base; offset 15 -> cross-16B sd
  li   t3, 0xDEADBEEF
  li   t5, 32                   # unique-line stride
.Lloop:
  sd   t3, 0(t0)                # first  cross-16B sd
  sd   t3, 16(t0)               # second cross-16B sd
  add  t0, t0, t5
  addi s2, s2, -1
  bnez s2, .Lloop
```

To rebuild from the attached `.S`:

```bash
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -nostdlib -nostartfiles -static \
    -march=rv64g -mabi=lp64 -T link.ld \
    -o unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.elf unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.S
riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy -O binary unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.elf unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.bin
```

`link.ld` is a one-line linker script placing `.text` at `0x80000000`.

[unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27475354/unalignq_enqptr_deqptr.zip) — contains the `.S`, the pre-built `.bin`, the linker script, and the failing run log.

### Additional context

_No response_
